findings.title: 当社サービスの一部システムに対する不正アクセスについて (IDC Frontier initial notice)
findings.summary_md: IDC Frontier's first notice, published October 7, 2026 per the advisory page (JST, date shown on the page), disclosed that unauthorized third-party access had caused an outage in part of its IDCF Cloud service starting around 03:40 that morning, with East Japan Region 1 as the affected scope. The company said affected customers were being contacted individually and that safety checks of other regions were underway.

findings.title: 【第2報】当社サービスの一部システムに対する不正アクセスについて (IDC Frontier second report)
findings.summary_md: The second advisory, dated October 7, 2026 on the page, confirmed the East Japan Region 1 outage was caused by a third-party ransomware attack and put the affected population at 495 companies and municipalities contracting IDCF Cloud. It stated network isolation and system shutdown were complete, identification of the intrusion route was ongoing, and management consoles in other regions had been shut off pending safety verification.

findings.title: 【第3報】当社サービスの一部システムへの不正アクセスによる障害について (IDC Frontier third report)
findings.summary_md: The third advisory, dated October 8, 2026 on the page, narrowed the impact to part of East Japan Region 1, specifically the tesla, henry, pascal, and joule zones, where virtual servers stopped and could not be restarted. It warned that customer data stored in those zones is expected to be difficult to extract or restore, with recovery possible only from backups customers hold themselves, and said the company had reported the incident to its supervising ministry and the Metropolitan Police. IDCF Cloud TypeS, formerly White Cloud ASPIRE, and IDCF Private Cloud were declared out of scope.
